drivingQuestion: What does 'and so too' add for a swarm of bees?
outcomeNote: the mishna needed 'and so too' to exclude unspecified despair even for bees

segments.he: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ נְחִיל שֶׁל דְּבוֹרִים, דְּקִנְיָן דְּרַבָּנַן הוּא. סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הַאי, כֵּיוָן דְּרַבָּנַן בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דְּקָנֵי לֵיהּ – אֲפִילּוּ סְתָמָא נָמֵי מִיָּיאַשׁ; קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: אִם נִתְיָיאֲשׁוּ הַבְּעָלִים – אֵין, אִי לָא – לָא.
segments.en: The Gemara explains: «This is» what «it is saying:» The halakha stated by the mishna applies «even» to «a swarm of bees, which is» the property of the owners via «a rabbinic» form of «acquisition» due to the fact that one cannot effect a legal acquisition of bees by Torah law. It might «enter your mind to say» that in «this» case, «since one acquires» the swarm of bees «only by rabbinic law, even» where the owners’ response is «unspecified» it can be assumed that they «despair» of recovering the bees, and the finder may keep them. To counter this, the mishna «teaches us» that «if» it is known that «the owners» of the bees «despaired» of recovering them, «yes,» the finder may keep the bees; «if» they did «not» despair, «no,» he may not keep them.
